fun_facts: A bluefish belongs to a family of exactly one species: Pomatomus saltatrix has no close living relatives, unusual for a fish this common and this widely fished.

Bluefish turn up almost everywhere in the world's temperate coastal waters, from the Mediterranean to Australia to South Africa, with one glaring gap: they've never established themselves along the Pacific coast of the Americas, and nobody has ever fully explained why.
A bluefish switches from eating plankton to eating other fish once it's barely three or four inches long, an unusually early and abrupt diet change for a predatory fish.
